To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following are true: (1) The patient is a person who is in a particular situation, who has particular attitudes and beliefs, and who is interacting with particular other people in a particular way; (2) the patient has certain physiological functions that are influenced by the above variables; (3) these physiological functions have a direct influence on the patient’s health; (4) the patient’s health is influenced indirectly by the above variables through their influence on the patient's physiological functions.

(1) the behavior of patients is not a cause but a correlate of physical disease, (2) the correlation of behavior with disease is neither perfect nor consistent, and (3) the behavior of a patient is a function of his or her past experiences and present social situation.

(1) a person's health is influenced by the way he or she perceives and copes with the environment, (2) the influence of psychosocial factors on the course of disease is mediated by physiological and behavioral mechanisms, (3) the mechanisms that connect psychosocial factors to the course of disease are not well understood, (4) there is an urgent need for well‐controlled studies that will clarify these mechanisms, and (5) such studies will require interdisciplinary cooperation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interplay of the social and physical environment with the individual, and the ways in which these interactions are reflected in the behavior of the individual, in his social interactions, and in the bodily tissues of the individual.
the study of the relationship between behavior and physical disease.
the relationship between behavior and disease, but the field has been so defined that we have not yet been able to discover the causal mechanisms involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of psychosomatic medicine is a promising field of study, but that the promise has not yet been realized.

psychosomatic medicine is a field of study in which the facts are few and the theories many; in which there is a lack of agreement as to what is meant by psychosomatic medicine; and in which there is little agreement on the methodology of the field, the goals of the research, or the nature of the mediating processes.
we do not really know what psychosomatic medicine is, what it is about, and what the future holds for the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the field is in a state of transition.
the study of psychosomatic medicine has not led to the development of effective therapeutic techniques for the alleviation of human suffering.
psychosomatic medicine is still an infant field that has not yet reached the stage of maturity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
psychosomatic medicine is a field of medicine, and as such it is not a subject but rather a point of view.
the mind is not an independent entity but is a product of the brain and is therefore subject to the same physical laws as the rest of the body.
psychosocial factors can be very influential in health and disease, but the mechanisms that link them to disease remain largely unknown.
